root_cause.text: The function `skb_is_err_queue()` incorrectly identified AF_PACKET outgoing tap skbs as error-queue skbs because it only checked `skb->pkt_type == PACKET_OUTGOING`, without verifying that the destructor is `sock_rmem_free`, which is set only for genuine error-queue skbs.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "skb_is_err_queue() treats PACKET_OUTGOING as the sole marker for an skb from sk_error_queue. That assumption is not true for AF_PACKET sockets: outgoing packet taps are also delivered to packet sockets with skb->pkt_type == PACKET_OUTGOING, but their skb->cb is owned by AF_PACKET instead of struct sock_exterr_skb." The patch modifies `skb_is_err_queue()` to also require `skb->destructor == sock_rmem_free`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add declaration of sock_rmem_free function to socket header.
intent_record.what: Added a new function declaration `void sock_rmem_free(struct sk_buff *skb);` in the header file after `void sock_rfree(struct sk_buff *skb);`.
intent_record.how: This change makes the `sock_rmem_free` function available for calls from other compilation units, enabling a new API for freeing receive memory associated with an skb.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove static qualifier from sock_rmem_free to make it accessible to other kernel modules.
intent_record.what: Removed the `static` keyword from the function definition of `sock_rmem_free`, changing its linkage from internal to external.
intent_record.how: The function `sock_rmem_free` is now globally visible and can be called from other kernel modules, whereas previously it was only accessible within the same compilation unit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update comment in skb_set_err_queue to clarify the purpose of setting pkt_type to PACKET_OUTGOING in relation to skb_is_err_queue() test and sock_rmem_free destructor.
intent_record.what: The comment inside skb_set_err_queue() was changed from explaining that it's safe to misuse pkt_type to mark error queue skbs because local sockets never have PACKET_OUTGOING, to explaining that the error-queue test in skb_is_err_queue() matches this marker with the destructor installed by sock_queue_err_skb().
intent_record.how: No functional impact; only the internal documentation comment is updated to better describe the relationship between the marker and the test/destructor.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix misidentification of error-queue skbs by adding a destructor check to disambiguate from AF_PACKET outgoing taps.
intent_record.what: Modified `skb_is_err_queue` to additionally check that `skb->destructor == sock_rmem_free` alongside the existing `skb->pkt_type == PACKET_OUTGOING` check, and updated the comment to explain the ambiguity.
intent_record.how: The function now returns true only when both conditions hold, ensuring that AF_PACKET outgoing tap skbs (which also use PACKET_OUTGOING) are not misidentified as error-queue skbs.
